Subject: Re: SLA for pilot — baseline uptime & monthly credit mechanics

Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — system looked solid. As we start contracting the pilot I wanted to get ahead of the SLA mechanics so legal & procurement can budget for potential remedies. A few specific asks from our side:

- Uptime baseline: we'd like to see 99.97% as the commitment for the hosted API (critical for our payments routing). Is that something you can commit to or provide an alternate ladder?
- Remedy calculation: we prefer pro-rata credits (minutes-of-downtime / total minutes * monthly invoice) rather than capped banding. Can you walk us through typical monthly caps?
- Maintenance carve-outs: our security team is wary of large maintenance carve-ins. We typically accept scheduled maintenance with 24hrs notice and no more than 4 hours/month. How do you usually handle advance notice and bucket size?
- Latency SLOs: aside from availability, we need a P95 tail under 250ms for inference across us-east. Is there a latency remedy or is it just availability tied to outage?

If you can share your standard SLA template and an illustration of how credits would flow month-to-month (worst, expected, and best-case), we can speed procurement sign-off.

Appreciate it — Evan
Evan Brooks

Evan — thanks for the clear list. Forwarding our recommendation and the draft template for your and procurement's review. High level summary below; attached is the PDF of the template and a simple spreadsheet you can drop your numbers into.

Summary of our recommended terms (pilot / hosted):
- Baseline availability: 99.95% availability per calendar month (standard).
- Tiered remedy bands (illustrative):
  * >= 99.95%: no remedy
  * 99.80% - 99.95%: 5% monthly service credit
  * 99.50% - 99.79%: 15% monthly service credit
  * < 99.50%: 30% monthly service credit (upper cap)
- Monthly cap: credits capped at 30% of that month’s invoice. We can discuss higher caps for enterprise deals on a case-by-case basis with commensurate pricing/commitment.
- Pro-rata overlay: we can offer pro-rata calculation on top of banding for the pilot if you need exact minute-level math — our calculator shows similar numeric outcomes but clearer audit trail for procurement.
- Maintenance carve-out: scheduled maintenance (planned by Redwood) is excluded if notified >= 48 hours AND duration per event <= 4 hours; aggregate scheduled maintenance not to exceed 8 hours/month for hosted pilots. For enterprise Dedicated deployments we can be more restrictive.
- Emergency maintenance/forced mitigations will be excluded if we can demonstrate CVE/zero-day remediation needs; we will notify as soon as possible and issue credit when remediation impacts availability beyond thresholds.
- Latency: we provide an operational latency target (P95 <= 250ms in us-east) but do not currently offer financial remedy tied to latency; availability is the financial trigger. For customers prioritizing tail latency, we recommend Dedicated pools and an addendum that ties specific latency regressions to remedies (we can draft language).
- Escrow / smoothing: to address procurement concerns about big one-off credits, we offer a credit-smoothing option where monthly credits beyond 15% are escrowed and distributed over up to 3 months (reduces abrupt bill volatility).

Next steps we propose:
1) We share the attached SLA-template-v1.pdf and credit-calculator.xlsx.
2) If procurement prefers a 24-hour maintenance notice instead of 48, we can offer that for this pilot but will limit aggregate monthly maintenance to 6 hours and add a short-term availability buffer of +0.02% (i.e., baseline 99.93%) to compensate.
3) If FinTechSquad requires P95 latency remedies, we can scope a latency addendum for Dedicated or a pilot SLA extension.

I'll leave technical questions to Ben and contract language to Laura (cc’d). Happy to hop on a call this week.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Quick technical clarification on latency and regional split. Evan / FinTechSquad —

- The P95 <= 250ms target is achievable from our us-east pool for typical 1-2k token requests. Tail latency above that often correlates with very long-sequence inference or heavy KV cache misses. If you have consistent sub-250ms needs at higher seq lengths, we should profile a representative workload.
- Regional availability: our template measures availability per-region; if you expect failover between regions (us-east -> us-west) we should define whether you want a single global availability metric or per-region metrics with fallback semantics. That affects how credits are triggered (a regional blip might not equal global outage).
- Batching/maintenance: during large maintenance we may evict caches resulting in a short spike in latency which doesn't always show up as availability loss. That’s another reason some customers want a latency addendum.

If you can share a sample production trace (anonymized) or typical request sizes, we can run it through our latency model and confirm the right SLO + remedy approach.

—Ben
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Rishi / Ben / Laura — thanks for the rapid follow-up and the attachments. A few items from procurement & ops after review: 

- Maintenance notice: procurement will accept a 48-hour notice but only if we can get the aggregate cap down to 6 hours/month per your suggested concession. We want an explicit clause that maintenance will be scheduled outside our 08:00–20:00 ET peak window unless agreed otherwise.
- Baseline: 99.95% is tolerable for the pilot if you agree to the credit-smoothing escrow approach. Procurement asked that escrowed credits be visible in our billing portal and automatically applied in the next billing cycle unless disputed.
- P1 response time: for incidents that cause availability deterioration beyond the second band (i.e., <99.80%), we require a P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes and a status every 30 minutes until resolution or mitigation. Can you add operational response commitments to the template?
- Critical incident uplift: for outages that impact payment processing (identified in-scope by both sides during onboarding), we want an uplifted remedy multiplier x1.5 for any band-triggered credits.

If you can incorporate those four items into a short redline and return it today/tomorrow we'll try to get the procurement queue moving. Happy to take a call — Evan (cc procurement).

Onwards,
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform Ops, FinTechSquad
